title: Mata v. Avianca — Rule 11 sanctions for fabricated ChatGPT citations
text: Attorney sanctioned $5,000 under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 11 for filing a brief citing six nonexistent cases fabricated by ChatGPT. First mainstream AI hallucination sanction. Candor to the tribunal and duty to verify authority.

title: ABA Formal Opinion 512 — Generative AI Tools
text: Maps existing Model Rules onto generative AI: competence, confidentiality, communication, supervision, meritorious claims, candor to the tribunal, reasonable fees. Lawyers must have a reasonable understanding of the tool's capabilities and limitations and must review output. Human review required.

title: Texas Ethics Opinion 705 on generative AI
source: Texas State Bar Professional Ethics Committee
text: State-level ethics guidance on lawyers' use of generative AI, echoing competence, confidentiality, and supervision duties.

title: Colorado repeals and replaces its AI Act (SB 26-189) — narrower transparency law
text: Colorado's landmark risk-based AI Act (SB 24-205) was repealed before its risk-management and impact-assessment duties ever took effect, and replaced by SB 26-189, a narrower automated-decisionmaking disclosure and consumer-rights law effective January 2027. The EU-style risk-based model retreats; the patchwork of state AI rules continues but tilts toward transparency. Colorado stays part of the multi-jurisdiction patchwork a firm must reconcile.

title: California Rule of Court 10.430 — courts must adopt generative-AI policies
text: The first statewide court rule on generative AI requires California courts to adopt AI-use policies covering confidentiality, accuracy, bias, disclosure, and human review of AI output, with no autonomous AI decisions. It spreads documented verification and disclosure discipline to the judiciary's own AI use, widening the governance patchwork courts and firms must reconcile.

title: Couvrette v. Wisnovsky — ~$110K penalty for 15 fake cases, 8 fabricated quotes
text: Largest known US AI-citation penalty: ~$110,204 across orders Dec 2025 and March 2026 against attorneys whose briefs contained 15 nonexistent cases and 8 fabricated quotations. Verify citation duty; candor.

title: New York Formal Opinion 2025-6 — recording/transcribing client meetings with AI
text: Guidance on AI recording and transcription of client meetings, emphasizing confidentiality and informed consent. Client data governance.

title: AI sanction wave: ~$145K in Q1 2026 penalties
text: Courts imposed roughly $145,000 in AI fake-citation sanctions in Q1 2026, including a record Oregon penalty and the first substantial federal appellate fine tied to AI-tainted briefs. 300+ judges now require AI disclosure in filings. Reasonable inquiry and verification.

title: Nebraska Supreme Court suspends attorney over hallucinated appeal brief
text: Attorney suspended after an appeal brief contained 57 of 63 defective citations including 20 hallucinated cases; disciplinary investigation ordered. Supervision and candor. The cover-up drew the harsher response across cases.

title: California updated Practical Guidance for Generative AI
text: Board approved updated practical guidance for the use of generative AI in the practice of law. Confidentiality, competence, disclosure.

title: Stanford: Westlaw AI 34% error rate, Lexis+ AI 17%
text: Stanford research documented hallucination/error rates of 34% for Westlaw AI-Assisted Research and 17% for Lexis+ AI. Hallucination rate becomes a measurable liability input for tool selection and a benchmark question. Competence in tool choice.

title: CNA adds AI-governance questionnaires to malpractice renewals
text: CNA introduced supplemental AI-usage questionnaires at renewal; firms unable to demonstrate AI governance face higher premiums or coverage restrictions. AXA XL offers an AI endorsement ~5-15% above base premium. An uncertified AI system trends toward uninsurable and therefore unusable. Insurers act as continuous private regulators.

title: EU AI Act obligations take effect
text: EU AI Act obligations for high-risk AI: conformity assessments, risk management systems, operational human oversight. Cross-jurisdiction convergence pressure on multinational legal departments.

title: AI AGENT Act would require scope-limited, revocable, logged agent authorization
text: Proposed AI AGENT Act would require covered AI agents to operate under transparent, documented, scope-limited, revocable user authorization and to keep records of their actions. Agentic supervision and UPL-by-proxy concerns.

title: Federal court excludes expert for AI-hallucinated citations
text: Court excluded an expert witness whose report contained AI-hallucinated citations, extending exposure beyond attorney briefs to expert work product. Verification duty broadens.

title: France criminalizes judicial profiling (Justice Reform Act, Art. 33)
text: France's Justice Reform Act Article 33 prohibits the use of analytics to predict or profile the decisions of individual named judges, with criminal penalties. First national ban on judicial analytics / judicial profiling; signals a regulatory direction for litigation outcome prediction and judge simulation.

title: England & Wales judiciary guidance — first formal AI guidance for judges
text: First guidance of its kind to judicial office holders, issued with the Lady Chief Justice and Master of the Rolls. Permits AI as a 'secondary tool' but says legal research and analysis is 'not recommended'; prohibits entering confidential or private information into public AI chatbots; requires independent verification of all AI output. Extends the disclosure and verification duty to a major common-law jurisdiction.

title: Stanford/Yale 'Large Legal Fictions' — 58–88% hallucination rate on legal queries
source: Dahl, Magesh, Suzgun & Ho (Journal of Legal Analysis)
text: Tested general-purpose LLMs against 15,000 federal court cases: hallucination rates of 58% (GPT-4) to 88% (Llama 2) on verifiable legal questions, rising with complexity and accompanied by systematic overconfidence. Foundational capability evidence that makes the error rate a measurable input to tool choice and the benchmark a compliance instrument.

title: Florida Bar Ethics Opinion 24-1 — self-learning AI and client confidentiality
source: The Florida Bar Board of Governors
text: One of the first state ethics opinions on generative AI. Requires due diligence into whether a tool is 'self-learning' (retains inputs for training data), informed client consent before disclosing confidential information to a third-party tool, and treats AI like a non-lawyer assistant for supervision. Anchors the no-training clause as an ethical default and confidentiality as a data governance question.

title: EU Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853 — software and AI are 'products'
text: In force December 8, 2024. Broadens 'product' to include software and AI systems regardless of supply mode, making AI providers subject to strict product liability as manufacturers. Non-compliance with the EU AI Act directly informs a finding of defectiveness; rebuttable presumptions of defect/causation ease the claimant's burden. A rare concrete shift of vendor liability onto AI suppliers rather than only the deploying lawyer.

title: New Jersey requires technology CLE including AI — competence as a program requirement
text: Approved April 2025; effective January 1, 2027. Mandates one technology-related continuing legal education credit every two years, explicitly including developments in AI. Converts technological competence from an aspirational duty into a standing training requirement, foreshadowing broader mandatory AI CLE.

title: AI LEAD Act (S.2937) — proposed federal AI product liability standards
text: Introduced September 29, 2025. Would create federal product liability causes of action for AI systems — defective design, failure to warn, breach of express warranty, strict liability — while barring Section 230 immunity and waiver clauses. A legislative push to place vendor liability and accountability on AI developers, not only on the deploying professional.

title: Virginia LEO 1901 — value-based billing need not shrink when AI cuts time
source: Supreme Court of Virginia / Virginia State Bar
text: Approved November 24, 2025. Holds that a lawyer is not ethically required to reduce a non-hourly, value-based billing fee merely because generative AI reduced the time spent. Diverges from ABA Formal Opinion 512's suggestion that charging the same flat fee may be unreasonable; efficiency gains, specialized AI skill, and professional judgment support fee reasonableness. Hourly billing must still reflect actual time. First state opinion squarely on AI and fee reasonableness.

title: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (TRAIGA) takes effect
text: Effective January 1, 2026. Comprehensive state AI law: intent-based prohibitions on discriminatory or manipulative AI, AG enforcement with $10,000–$200,000 penalties and a 60-day cure period, no private right of action, plus a regulatory sandbox and safe harbor. Deepens the patchwork of state AI regulation that forces multi-jurisdiction firms toward one operating model.

title: Withers v. Aberdeen — both sides sanctioned, four lawyers removed for AI hallucinations
text: Attorneys for both parties filed submissions containing hallucinated citations. The court revoked two pro hac vice admissions (two-year bar) and disqualified two local counsel, fining them; one attorney's claim of not knowing AI could hallucinate was found 'incredulous.' The underlying dispute concerned reasonable attorney fees. Hardens verification and disclosure duties and rejects ignorance as a defense.

title: Stanford RegLab 'Hallucination-Free?' — RAG legal research tools still hallucinate 17–34%
source: Magesh, Surani, Dahl, Suzgun, Manning & Ho (Stanford RegLab)
text: First preregistered empirical benchmark of purpose-built, retrieval-augmented legal AI tools (Lexis+ AI, Westlaw AI-Assisted Research, Ask Practical Law): each hallucinated on 17% to 34% of queries despite vendor 'hallucination-free' marketing. Confident, well-cited but wrong answers are the dominant failure mode. The authors conclude responsible use demands careful human review and independent verification of every AI output — attestation that 'a human reviewed it' is insufficient when the error is a plausible fabricated citation. Establishes both the error-rate benchmark and the verification duty as measurable capability facts.

title: A&O Shearman puts agentic AI to work firm-wide, revenue-sharing with Harvey
text: A major global firm deployed agentic AI agents at production scale across antitrust, cyber, fund formation and loan review, licensing the tools to clients and rival firms under a revenue-share with Harvey. Multi-step autonomous agent work on live matters shows scope-limited agentic deployment is available and being adopted at scale today, not just promised.

title: PLI launches the first legal-AI competency framework
text: Practising Law Institute launched the first industry AI competency framework (May 2026), giving firms and lawyers a defined standard to train against and measure AI competence. A usable competency standard firms can build their training and governance program on is now on the shelf.

title: E-discovery and contract review are the most mature, most-trusted legal-AI uses, now at scale
text: E-discovery and contract review are the two most mature legal-AI uses and among the most trusted (roughly 95% report trusting e-discovery AI; contract-review adoption growing fast). Reliable, verifiable review runs at production scale inside firms, so the verification-and-audit controls around AI work product can be stood up with proven tooling.

title: Enterprise legal-AI vendors bind no-training and ship data-governance / attestation controls
text: Enterprise legal-AI vendors contractually bind no-training on client data and offer deployable data-governance, retention, and vendor-attestation controls. The confidentiality control (data-flow mapping + vendor attestation) can be stood up by buying from vendors who already meet the bar.

title: vLex Vincent AI launched (GPT-4)
text: vLex shipped Vincent AI, a GPT-4 legal-research assistant. First-of-kind research-AI launch; the vendor research-tooling trajectory begins.

title: Claude 2.1: 200K context + beta tool use
text: Claude 2.1 raised the context window to 200K tokens and introduced beta tool use. A frontier-model unlock legal tooling builds on (long-document review).

title: Claude 3: first Claude vision/document input
text: Claude 3 added vision and document input, letting legal tooling read scanned filings and exhibits natively.

title: Claude 3.5 Sonnet: first frontier computer-use public beta
text: First frontier public beta of computer use — an AI that operates a computer. The substrate for agentic legal tooling that acts, not just drafts.

title: Harvey Series D ~$100M at $3B, Sequoia-led
text: Harvey raised a ~$100M Series D at a $3B valuation on fast ARR growth and roughly half the Am Law 100 as customers. Capital at this scale funds the next tier of agentic and research tooling.

title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet hybrid reasoning + Claude Code preview
text: Claude 3.7 Sonnet added hybrid reasoning and shipped Claude Code in research preview — reasoning and coding the vendor agentic tooling builds on.

title: OpenAI Responses API + Agents SDK: third-party agentic/computer-use
text: OpenAI shipped the Responses API and Agents SDK, letting third parties build agentic/computer-use systems. Legal vendors can now assemble agents on OpenAI's stack.

title: LRAGE: legal RAG gains are corpus/backbone-dependent, not monotonic
text: Peer-reviewed study: legal retrieval-augmented-generation gains depend on the corpus and backbone, not monotonic scaling — domain-specific corpora outperform. Refines the capability claim behind retrieval-based legal tooling.

title: Claude Code GA (1.0.0)
text: Claude Code reached general availability — a production agentic coding tool. Proof of the agentic substrate that legal agentic tooling extends.

title: OpenAI Operator upgraded to o3, global research preview
text: OpenAI upgraded Operator to the o3 model and opened a global research preview of browser-driving agents. Agentic substrate widening across the two frontier labs.

title: Harvey Series E $300M at $5B, Kleiner Perkins/Coatue
text: Harvey raised a $300M Series E at a $5B valuation. Escalating valuation on the same revenue base concentrates more build capacity in agentic and research tooling.

title: Clio signs definitive agreement to acquire vLex ($1B)
text: Clio signed a definitive agreement to acquire research provider vLex for $1B, pairing practice management with legal research. Tool-surface consolidation toward one operating model.

title: Vals legal_bench: GPT-5 84.6%, #1 of 63 models
text: Vals' legal_bench snapshot ranked GPT-5 at 84.6% atop 63 models on legal reasoning. A vendor benchmark — a measured-but-vendor-sourced error signal, not an independent certification.

title: Ebers 'LawGPT': UPL-by-LLM a live comparative question
source: Cambridge Handbook of Generative AI and the Law
text: Scholarly chapter frames unauthorized-practice-by-LLM as a live comparative question, constraining what non-lawyer vendors may ship without bar authorization.

title: Claude 1M-token context public beta (Sonnet 4)
text: Claude opened a 1M-token context public beta — whole-case-record scale. Stretches what a single competent review pass can hold.

title: JURIX 2025: frontier LLMs era-biased and citation-hallucinating (GPT-5 35.29% pre-1881)
text: Peer-reviewed JURIX study: frontier LLMs are era-biased and citation-hallucinating, scoring 35.29% (GPT-5) on pre-1881 authority and 73.31% best on overruling-identification. Quantifies the verification duty as a measured capability fact.

title: Harvey Series F ~$160M at $8B, a16z-led; cumulative >$1B
text: Harvey raised ~$160M at an $8B valuation, the decacorn-scale round for a legal-AI pure-play. The capital now on hand funds a full agentic product line, not just research.

title: Legora Series C $150M at $1.8B
text: Legora raised a $150M Series C at a $1.8B valuation for agentic legal workflow. A second agentic-workflow pure-play enters the capital escalation.

title: Clio closes vLex ($1B) + $500M Series G (NEA) at $5B
text: Clio closed the $1B vLex acquisition and announced a $500M Series G at a $5B valuation, cementing practice-management-plus-research as one converged platform.

title: Legora Series D $550M at $5.55B, Accel-led
text: Legora raised a $550M Series D at a $5.55B valuation, tripling its prior round in months. Agentic-workflow capital compounding.

title: Claude 1M context GA (Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6)
text: Claude 1M-token context reached GA (media limit 100 to 600 pages). Whole-record review becomes a standard capability, not a beta.

title: Harvey Series G ~$200M at $11B, GIC+Sequoia; ~$190M ARR
text: Harvey raised ~$200M at an $11B valuation on ~$190M ARR. Legal-AI pure-play reaches eleven-figure scale; build capacity continues to concentrate.

title: Legora ~$50M extension (Nvidia NVentures+Atlassian) + 5 acquisitions
text: Legora added ~$50M (Nvidia NVentures + Atlassian) and made five acquisitions (Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, Wexler), consolidating an M&A-led workflow suite.

title: EU Digital Omnibus: Annex III high-risk deferred to 2026-12-02, Annex I to 2028-08-02
text: The EU Digital Omnibus deferred Annex III high-risk obligations to 2026-12-02 and Annex I to 2028-08-02, widening the runway for legal-AI vendors before conformity-assessment duties bind.

title: Etymolt trademark-clearance hallucination benchmark
text: Etymolt published a trademark-clearance hallucination benchmark (five metrics vs USPTO TSDR). A vendor-authored measured error signal — useful, but self-described.

title: EU Commission draft: agentic/coordinating systems = single high-risk system (anti-splitting)
text: Commission draft guidance would treat agentic/coordinating systems as a single high-risk system, closing the anti-splitting loophole. Tightens what vendors may ship as agentic legal systems.

title: Claude computer-use + browser-use GA (toolsets 20260801)
text: Claude computer-use and browser-use reached GA. Agentic substrate is now generally available for legal vendors to build multi-step autonomous tooling on.

title: Thomson Reuters agrees to acquire Casetext $650M cash (closed 2023-08-17)
text: Thomson Reuters agreed to acquire Casetext for $650M cash, folding CoCounsel into its research stack. A deep-pocketed incumbent absorbing a legal-AI research tool consolidates benchmark-and-verification tooling as the default build surface.

title: Robin AI $26M Series B, Temasek-led (CLM/workflow)
text: Robin AI raised a $26M Series B led by Temasek for contract-review/CLM tooling. Contract-lifecycle build capital; self-reported single-source round.

title: Luminance $40M Series B, March Capital-led (CLM)
text: Luminance raised a $40M Series B led by March Capital for contract-analysis/CLM tooling. Contract-review build capital.

title: Leya $25M Series A, Redpoint-led (agentic research)
text: Leya raised a $25M Series A led by Redpoint for an agentic legal-research assistant. Research-plus-agentic build capital.

title: Relativity aiR for Review GA (genAI e-discovery)
text: Relativity shipped aiR for Review at GA, bringing genAI to e-discovery review. Vendor build proof in the verification/evidence space; no funding round attached.

title: EvenUp $135M Series D, Bain Capital Ventures, $1B+ unicorn (PI claims)
text: EvenUp raised a $135M Series D led by Bain Capital Ventures at a $1B+ valuation for personal-injury claims workflow. Agentic claims-processing build capital.

title: Paxton AI $22M Series A, Unusual Ventures, total $28M (research/drafting)
text: Paxton AI raised a $22M Series A led by Unusual Ventures for research and drafting. Benchmark-and-verification build capital.

title: Luminance $75M Series C, Point72-led, valuation undisclosed (CLM)
text: Luminance raised a $75M Series C led by Point72 Private Investments; valuation not disclosed. Contract-analysis/CLM build capital at scale.

title: Spellbook $50M Series B, Khosla-led, $350M post-money (contract + agentic drafting)
text: Spellbook raised a $50M Series B led by Khosla at a $350M post-money for contract review plus agentic drafting. Self-reported single-source round.

title: Spellbook $40M RBCx debt facility to fund acquisitions (acquirer, not acquired)
text: Spellbook secured a $40M RBCx debt facility to acquire smaller generative-legal vendors (up to $60M/five deals). M&A-led consolidation in contract-review tooling.

title: Park v. Kim (2d Cir.) — referral for AI-produced nonexistent case
text: Second Circuit referred attorney Jae S. Lee to its Grievance Panel under Local Rule 46.2 for citing a nonexistent AI-produced case (Matter of Bourguignon v. Coordinated Behavioral Health Servs., 114 A.D.3d 947) that she admitted did not exist. Earliest circuit-level AI-citation referral in the set; verification duty extends to appellate practice.

title: Missouri Informal Opinion 2024-11 — pre-ABA generative-AI guidance
source: Office of Legal Ethics Counsel, Supreme Court of Missouri
text: Non-binding advisory guidance issued three months ahead of ABA Op 512, mapping generative AI onto existing rules: competence (4-1.1, self-education and verifying AI output before reliance), confidentiality (4-1.6, reviewing platform terms and input handling), candor (4-3.3), and supervision of nonlawyer assistants (4-5.3).

title: Illinois Supreme Court AI policy — disclosure of AI use NOT required in pleadings
text: Statewide policy holding professional-conduct rules fully apply to AI use, users must review AI content for accuracy before submission, AI must not compromise confidential information, and disclosure of AI use is deliberately NOT required in pleadings to avoid a chilling effect. A disclosure-fault-line counterpoint showing the patchwork has not converged; some individual circuit judges later issued contrary standing orders.

title: Mezu v. Mezu (Md. App.) — AGC referral for non-lawyer clerk AI delegation
source: Appellate Court of Maryland (No. 361 Sept. Term 2025)
text: First-time Maryland appellate treatment of attorney AI misuse: court referred appellee's attorney to the Attorney Grievance Commission for a brief replete with citation irregularities including fabricated ChatGPT cases (11 irregular among 27; four nonexistent), publishing as a warning to others. The failure mode was delegation — the attorney's non-lawyer clerk used ChatGPT for research and the attorney relied on the clerk's summaries without reading the cited cases.

title: Amarsingh v. Frontier Airlines (10th Cir.) — $1,000 FRAP 38 + bar referral
text: Tenth Circuit sanctioned a Maryland-licensed pro se lawyer $1,000 under FRAP 38 for an appellate brief with seven fabricated ChatGPT-generated citations, and referred the order to Maryland disciplinary authorities. Federal sanction coupled with bar referral; verification duty hardening at the circuit level.

title: Alabama State Bar Public Reprimand of Matthew Reeves (Butler Snow)
text: First resolved state-bar disciplinary outcome tied to the Manasco N.D. Ala. federal sanction: Public Reprimand with General Publication for using ChatGPT to draft two motions containing fabricated citations he failed to verify (RPC 1.1, 3.3, 8.4(d), 8.4(g)). Bar discipline closes the loop the federal sanction opened.

title: Whiting v. City of Athens (6th Cir.) — two lawyers $15k each + double costs + referral
text: Two Tennessee lawyers sanctioned for a brief that repeatedly misrepresented the record and cited non-existent cases; each fined $15,000, jointly ordered to pay double costs and reimburse the appellees' full appellate fees, and referred to disciplinary proceedings.

title: California COPRAC — AI duties woven into six Rules of Professional Conduct
text: COPRAC approved a package converting advisory guidance into enforceable Rules of Professional Conduct by weaving AI obligations into six rules (1.1, 1.4, 1.6, 3.3, 5.1, 5.3): independently review and verify ANY AI output, disclose on significant risk or material effect on scope/cost, and verify cited authorities are not fabricated or taken out of context. First state bar to propose enforceable (not merely advisory) AI-specific rules; in a second comment round as of Sept 2026, not final.

title: Gamez v. County of Fresno (E.D. Cal.) — OSC names legal-AI product OpenCase
text: Magistrate judge issued an order to show cause after an opposition brief cited nonexistent authority and fabricated quotes, stating it suggests the attorney relied on generative artificial intelligence. The attorney attributed the false citations to the named legal-AI product OpenCase, used to refine and cite-check a general-AI draft. First OSC naming a specific legal-AI product as the source of fabricated citations — the first vendor-liability datapoint in the docket feed.
